text:
Lena Ortiz: FYI during the q5b int8-fast rollout the codegen promptset golden started showing a weird drift: small syntax differences (extra spaces before parens, missing trailing newlines) caused automatic dedupe to miss anchors and labellers to disagree.
Tom Brewer: can you share an example diff and the commit that flipped the kernel?
Lena Ortiz: rolled kernel cf9d2e (int8-fast-opt). example pair below from golden slice 17: 
```
expected: def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n
got: def add (a, b):\n    return a + b\n```
small but enough to change fingerprint and cause label mismatch.
Priya Nair: interesting. that smells like tokenization or generation spacing semantics changed by the quant kernel's temperature scaling (we saw token emission gaps earlier). did we change tokenizer or decode config?
Lena Ortiz: decode config unchanged. only kernel swap. we ran a token-level diff on a random subset and saw ~4.7% whitespace-token boundary deltas.
Carlos M.: annotation-bot just flagged a bump in "duplicate-miss" alerts on the ingest pipeline, same timeframe.
annotation-bot: 34 tasks with fingerprint mismatch reassigned to anchors-team (ids: 8021..8054).
Tom Brewer: action plan: (1) run micro-canary with previous kernel on a small ingest pool and compare golden-anchor recall; (2) add a CI check that rejects kernel swaps if the golden-set whitespace-token-delta > 2%; (3) surface diffs in labeling UI so labelers see both renderings.
Priya Nair: +1 on UI diffs. labelers were resolving these as "different code" which is noisy. if we show both variants they can fast-accept.
Lena Ortiz: starting canary revert: `deployctl set-kernel --model=q5b --kernel=cf2a11 --pool=canary-anchors` now. will kick off golden-scan.
Tom Brewer: also please capture the tokenizer token sequences for a failing sample: `curate inspect --id 8030 --tokens --show-render` so we can confirm whether whitespace tokens changed or decode whitespace insertion differs.
Lena Ortiz: sample 8030 tokens: `["def"," ","add","(","a",","," ","b",")",":"]` under cf9d2e vs `["def","add","(","a",",","b",")",":","\n"]` under cf2a11. note extra space tokens and missing newline token.
Carlos M.: that explains fingerprint drift. our dedupe hash ignores whitespace by default but the ingest preprocessor changed last quarter to be hash-sensitive for code (to preserve formatting). small change in kernel now breaks that guardrail.
Priya Nair: two proposals: (A) revert the formatting-sensitive hashing until we have kernel-stable invariants, or (B) normalize whitespace at fingerprinting time for code prompts and store normalized->raw mapping for display.
Tom Brewer: prefer (B) since we want to preserve formatting when humans care, but not let tiny kernel differences break dedupe. implement normalization as a preprocessing step that still surfaces raw variants to labelers.
Lena Ortiz: golden-scan results: canary with cf2a11 recovered anchor recall 0.963 vs 0.881 on cf9d2e slice. rolling back kernel on q5b for now.
annotation-bot: CI job 22011 completed: golden-scan summary attached.
Priya Nair: next steps: (1) add `kernel-impact` job to onboarding pipeline that compares normalized and raw hashes across kernels; (2) add a small golden-format-suite for code (20 samples) to gate kernel swaps; (3) update curation docs with guidance on fingerprint policies for code vs natural language.
Tom Brewer: I'll create the onboarding checklist PR and the `kernel-impact` job. Lena please add the 20 sample golden-format-suite to `gs://curation/gold/code-format-suite` and include expected normalized hashes.
Lena Ortiz: uploaded 20 cases and PR here: https://git.internal/redwood/curate/pulls/1459  includes normalization script and CI job.
Carlos M.: tagging eng-runtime so future kernel performance wins don't silently cause curation churn.
Tom Brewer: nice work. schedule a short retro tomorrow 9:30 to finalize whether hashing policy or kernel decoding should be primary source of truth.
Lena Ortiz: added calendar invite. thanks all. :thumbsup:
